target_customer: Employers hiring entry-level staff in India (sales, support, operations) who pay per hire; users are fresh graduates, mostly from tier II to IV cities
problem: Freshers in India lack interview preparation and job-ready skills, and employers struggle to hire entry-level talent at volume. Able coached candidates and placed them.
business_model: Placement fee charged to employers, roughly one month of salary per hire; training free to candidates

founders.name: Ravish Agrawal
founders.background_notes: Growth marketing background; described Able as his third attempt at solving education problems.

founders.name: Svatantra Kumar
founders.background_notes: Later founded WhatBytes per YC page.

founders.name: Siddharth Srivastava
founders.background_notes: Joined Instawork as a product leader after the acquisition.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app with content, mock interviews and job matching; standard consumer software for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Job and training platforms in India were crowded and employer relationships were the only real moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large incumbent copied it; staffing company Instawork acquired it in August 2024.

market_need_then: Large numbers of graduates entered the Indian job market each year with weak interview skills, and employers needed high-volume entry-level hires; the founders began by coaching over WhatsApp and saw thousands of responses in a day.

branding.community_and_virality: Started as WhatsApp coaching groups that reached thousands of people; no merch or fan communities found.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by Indian startup press but no sources show the brand itself driving growth; the name is generic and shares words with common terms.

outcome_analysis: Able grew from WhatsApp interview coaching into an app for freshers, raised a $1.8M seed in August 2020 and claimed millions of users and tens of thousands placed. It was acquired by Instawork in August 2024 for an undisclosed sum with investors exiting, a modest outcome without a clear venture-scale return, and its funding after the seed is not well documented.
notes: Seed sources: YourStory, People Matters. Some later reports cite $2.3M total and Elevation Capital as an investor; timing of Elevation's round not found, so not recorded. Company site fetch returned no content. Competitor sources are not dated to early 2020, so source_date is null. Placement counts vary by source. Apna (founded 2019) and Internshala were competitors but no sources dated to early 2020 were found, so the list is empty.
